notes:
Snapshot: Global trading desk (equities + options) exploring Dedicated capacity for inference. Goal: embed LLM features into trader workflow (real-time assistant), market data retrieval via embeddings, and fast reranking for signal prioritization.

Firmographics / constraints:
- Regulated finance firm, strict residency + audit needs. prefer US/UK data residency for trading data.
- Treasury requires net-30 billing + invoice format; procurement demands SLA clauses tied to penalties.

Technical targets and requirements (from SE workshops):
- Workload mix: 60% trading assistant (chat), 30% embedding search (historical market data), 10% reranking (signals).
- Latency SLO: P99 tail target for assistant < 60ms; ideal P90 ~ 20-30ms during market hours. Procurement pushing for 99.95% availability.
- Throughput: peak bursts up to ~1,200 TPS (small queries during open-market spikes), steady-state 200-400 QPS.
- Avg tokens per assistant call: 60-120 tokens (prompt + short completion). Reranking calls smaller (~30 tokens). Embeddings batch sizes mix 1-8 vectors.
- Model preference: want an LLM compatible with low-latency variant (quantized H100/A100-optimized) and an embeddings model with deterministic cost profile. Open to Redwood-curated model variants.

Reserved capacity / sizing discussion notes (working assumptions):
- Candidate hardware: H100-80GB or equivalent; aiming to commit 8 GPUs initially for Dedicated pool in US-East.
- Unit economics assumptions used in internal model:
  * Baseline GPU cost (list) assumed $11,000/GPU/month (vendor blended).
  * Slotting & infra overhead ~20% on top of raw GPU cost.
  * Estimated average utilization 55% (conservative) to 75% (optimistic) after batching and KV caching.
  * Effective tokens/sec per GPU (in production mix): ~6k-12k tokens/sec depending on model/sequence length.
  * Avg tokens/request ~ 90 -> implies ~66-133 reqs/sec worth per GPU under batch-friendly patterns.
- Commit scenarios modeled: 8 GPUs / 16 GPUs / 32 GPUs. Modeled monthly cost, expected utilization uplift from Redwood Optimize, and projected unit cost per 1M tokens.
- Example unit-econ excerpt (illustrative numbers from model):
  * 8 GPU commit, 55% util -> blended cost ~ $110k/month -> ~ $0.38 per 1k tokens -> $380 per 1M tokens.
  * 16 GPU commit, 70% util -> blended cost ~ $200k/month -> ~ $0.22 per 1k tokens -> $220 per 1M tokens.
  * 32 GPU commit, 75% util -> blended cost ~ $380k/month -> ~ $0.12 per 1k tokens -> $120 per 1M tokens.
- Notes: numbers are sensitive to tails/peak-hours; caching and routing to cheaper model variants reduces marginal cost. We stressed model switch fallbacks for degraded capacity scenarios.

SLA / commercial negotiation points:
- Procurement wants explicit P99 latency SLOs with financial penalties; Redwood must propose measurement windows and realistic SLOs for 99th percentile vs 99.9th.
- Requested: on-call escalation matrix, quarterly SLA review, audit rights, and detailed incident playbook.
- Pricing asks: discount tiers for multi-quarter commits + flexible bursting to hosted pool during unplanned peaks. They want a defined overage rate and ability to trade commit level at 6mo intervals.

POC plan & milestones:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): small sandbox on Dedicated 2-GPU pool to validate latency profile and average tokens/sec; run synthetic market bursts.
- Phase 2 (4-6 weeks): expanded POC on 8-GPU cluster with real ingestion of historical trade data (anonymized) and compare tail latencies with Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + caching).
- Phase 3 (8-12 weeks): pilot across one trading desk with canary routing, canary SLA, and runbook for fallbacks to hosted API if Dedicated pool saturates.

Decision criteria / risks:
- Will sign if Redwood can show: predictable P99 latency during market hours, unit cost per 1M tokens < $200 at committed volumes, and contract terms that satisfy procurement (billing + SLO language).
- Major risk: real-world utilization higher than modeled during market events -> needing additional GPUs or unacceptable tails. Procurement also wants data-residency proofs and SOC2 attestation.

Quote / paraphrase from CTO: "We need predictable cost per trade at scale — if you can show the math and the guarantees, we'll move fast."

Short-term next steps (CRM action items):
- AE to deliver detailed sizing spreadsheet with 3 commit scenarios and per-token economics by 2026-03-15.
- SE to run 48-hr synthetic spike test on 4-GPU sandbox and upload results (linked_fireflies).
- Schedule procurement + legal call to review SLA language week of 2026-03-22.
